recipes.name: Super-Delicious Zuppa Toscana
ingredients_raw: 4 slices bacon, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
0.25 bunch fresh spinach, tough stems removed

steps.text: Cook Italian sausage and red pepper flakes in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until crumbly, browned, and no longer pink, 10 to 15 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Cook bacon in the same Dutch oven over medium heat until crisp, about 10 minutes.
Drain, leaving a few tablespoons of drippings with the bacon in the bottom of the Dutch oven. Stir in onions and garlic; cook until onions are soft and translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add potatoes and simmer until fork tender, about 20 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium; stir in cream, cooked sausage, and spinach.
Cook and stir until spinach has wilted and sausage is warmed through; serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Super-Delicious Zuppa Toscana
raw_recipe.description: Zuppa Toscana made with sausage, potatoes, cream, spinach, and red pepper flakes. Tastes just like the one at your local Italian chain restaurant.

video.description: A rich soup made with sausage, potatoes, and cream.

review.reviewBody: I can't get enough of this soup! I tweaked it by leaving out the bacon and using kale instead of spinach (the famous restaurant uses kale). I also added 1 teaspoon of fennel as I think that it is crucial to the flavor of the soup. My Italian sausage was hot enough without the added red pepper, also. Still, I think this recipe is pretty forgiving and you can add or subtract to your taste. This was just what I was looking for to start me on my way to my new favorite soup. I also loved how quickly everything cooked.

This is very similar to a recipe that I make. I use hot sausage instead of mild, no hot pepper flakes, only 2-4 russett potatoes (depending on the size)sliced thin and they hold their shape and do not come out mushy and kale. You can substitute cauliflower for the potatoes for a lower carb diet and it is just as delicious. Definately just crumble the bacon instead of cutting into pieces. This is a crowd pleaser and my family loves it when I make this recipe!

I made this soup last night. I used Johnsonville Sweet Basil Italian sausage (which I LOVE) and Campbells chicken broth. It turned out EXTREMELY salty. I can handle a lot of salt in my food, and this was too salty, even for me. I added extra cream, just to try and tone down some of the saltiness. Maybe it might be better with reduced sodium ingredients, but I will not be making this again. Thanks anyways!

My favorite soup by far! Try the recipe as is first! Wonderful to double or quadruple recipe for freezing. To freeze: After step 2, add the sausage & red pepper back in with bacon, onion & garlic. Mix & let cool, put meat mixture into freezer bag. Thaw when ready to use. Use chicken soup base to make broth & heat like step 3 only waiting to put the meat mixture back in after the potatoes have cooked. Reduce heat & continue with heavy cream & spinach. Enjoy!! Thank-You souporsweets!!!

Excellent soup that I will make many times! My husband and I thought it was fantastic. A couple of notes: 1) there is no salt and pepper listed. Since I use broth with either no or reduced sodium, it definitely needed 3/4-1 tsp of salt. The pepper also added flavor. 2) like others I used kale instead of spinach since it's more authentic and adds more texture too. I did a fairly fine chop of curly kale so it would soften enough at the end and not be a big hunk on the spoon. 4-5 leaves equaled around two cups and that was a good amount for us. 3) I used hot Italian sausage instead of mild and omitted the red pepper flakes. 4) after reading comments, I also added about 3/4-1 tsp of fennel seeds to the sausage when I browned it and that flavor really punched up the flavor. Someone also suggested red wine vinegar so I drizzled some into the onions while they cooked, 1 tsp, maybe a little more? 5) since it was a lot more than 2 of will eat within a few days, I did not add the cream with the sausage and kale. I instead cooked the soup until it was done, spooned out half to freeze and then added 1/2 cup of cream and finished warming it. Cream soups don't seem to survive the freezer very well so I'll add cream after it's thawed and warmed. 6) we of course added freshly grated Parmesan cheese because everything is better with cheese :-) This is an easy recipe, it came together in the time listed and when served with bread, it made a perfect weeknight dinner with enough to freeze for another week! Future tweak - Family members have a mix of dairy intolerance and aversion to pork so I am going to try this with turkey sausage, turkey bacon and a good dairy-free "cream" and see how it turns out. I'll post how that turns out. ---Sorry this reads like a book. There is no way to break it into paragraphs

This soup is super easy and DELICIOUS. I use kale instead of spinach. Before you scoff at kale, you can give the kale a salt water bath to get rid of the bitterness and add the kale when you add the potatoes. Salt water bath - the washed & ready to use kale is easiest, take the kale and place into a large bowl of cold water and salt. Massage the kale in the salt water for maybe 30 seconds (you can let it sit in the salt water a little even after massaging it), drain and place into soup with potatoes. The crowd favorite is also when I use 1/2 hot Italian sausage and 1/2 sweet sausage (remove casing). Another great tip - use the small gold potatoes (cut in half’s or quarters depending of the size of potatoes you want). The yellow/gold potatoes pair better with all the ingredients.

This was amazing! Better than OG!! I doubled the pork and the kale because I like a hearty soup. I slow cooked this soup for 4 hours on high in my Insant Pot. I followed the directions through step 2 then added all ingredients (but only half of the kale) aside from the cream. When it was done I added in the other half of the kale and the cream and let it cook for 20 more minutes. The reason for adding the kale at different times was I wanted a mix of softer and then some that was a bit more crunchy. Absolutely delicious!

This 'new to us' soup was easy to make and a major hit. Because we were taking it to someone's house the next day it had plenty of time to 'meld' overnight in the fridge~ I think that is key in encouraging flavor development. Instead of adding salt I added a teaspoon of better than boullion which intensifies the richness of the broth nicely. Next time if I am taking it somewhere to reheat I will wait on adding the cream and do it there. We did add a teaspoon of fennel seeds in the last stages of cooking the sausage. Perfect! And we opted to up the texture by using kale instead of spinach. Excellent! I really like being able to control the spiciness of the sausage too! Had considered using the hot italian sausage but this way it was somewhere in between, We served with crusty french bread and a little sweet cream butter. Lovely, satisfying and definitely a new favorite!
I followed the recipe however instead of potatoes, cut up a head of cauliflower and add it in place of the potatoes.. ..cuts out carbs and it is absolutely delicious!

This is one of my go-to soups! I also use Kale (removing the stalks) instead of spinach. And, I put it all in a crockpot because I always double the recipe...but, I do cook the sausage first along with the onions/bacon. I use Bob Evans Zesty Hot sausage and then forget the red pepper flakes. I then put in the rest of the ingredients into the crockpot for several hours on low. Make this in the morning and have a wonderful soup ready for dinner! It also freezes well. Enjoy!

I was SO excited to make this soup because I love the Olive Garden version. This was nothing like it. I followed the directions exactly-only subbing kale for spinach and adding more potatoes (8) and sausage (1.5lbs) because we like a chunky soup and I read reviews that this was thin. I sliced 2 of the potatoes thinner so they could cook down to thicken the soup and the rest I sliced medium thickness so they wouldn't cook away. When the soup was ready I tasted it and it was SO thin and bland. It tasted like red pepper flake-flavored, watery chicken broth. I took about 2 ladle fulls of the soup out (sausage, taters and all)and blended a quick roux with some cornstarch and an extra large baked potato. It was still SO thin and tasteless--the chicken broth flavor was really overwhelming. Finally to salvage dinner (and a lot of leftovers) I added about 2 cups of potato flakes. I added them slowly and whisked to avoid clumping. This thickened the soup up beautifully and really cut the chicken broth taste. I bet after cooling overnight, the leftovers will soak up a lot of the broth so I suggest starting with just one cup of potato flakes so the flavor and thickness doesn't overwhelm and add more the next day if needed. I gave this a 2 stars because as directed it was pretty much unedible. Adding the potato flakes made it 3.5 (had a bit more "mashed potato flavor" than OG's soup) but I bet with some playing around with the potato flakes this could be a 4-5 star recipe.
Made half for family of 3 and everyone likes it. Added a little parmesan cheese to individual bowls
So good.....taste like it cam from olive garden....used Kayle in place of spinach
Would have given the 5 stars but the zuppa is made with kale i used that instead for a more authentic zuppa Tuscany
This is so good, taste just like the restaurant.
I made this for a party and there was nothing left! I used 1/2 and 1/2 instead of cream and the substitution was yummy. I will definitely make it again!
I thought I had crushed red pepper, but I didn’t, so I substituted 1/4 tsp of cayenne. Also added 1/2 of a 10 oz bag of spinach. It was delicious. Husband had two big bowls. Definitely a keeper.
Didn’t have heavy cream..used half and half. Didn’t have ground sausage..cut up Italian sausage links. This is delicious!
Very delicious! The recipe moves pretty quickly so definitely have all ingredients chopped and ready to go before starting. Will make again.

I eat Zuppa Toscana all the time and this is not made with Spinach but Kale. Don't know where they came up with all the onions either. There is none of that in there. The Italian sausage is what gives the soup all it's flavor and with the cream and chicken broth and red pepper flakes, this soup is wonderful. Go back and eat it again.
